rationale: PINS Node builtin classification, subpath forms included. The analyzer's builtin table was a flat list of bare module names, so every subpath Node actually ships — node:fs/promises, node:test, stream/promises, node:readline/promises, timers/promises, util/types, assert/strict, path/posix — fell through to `external:<specifier>` and the index claimed a dependency on an npm package named 'fs/promises' or 'test'. `node:test` is a bare name missing from the table itself, not a subpath, so both halves are pinned: the table entries (test/sqlite/sea/diagnostics_channel) and the subpath head rule. ANTI-POLLUTION: `lodash/merge` has exactly the shape of a builtin subpath and must stay external, and `express` is the plain bare-package control. The `imports` relationship pin proves the EDGE (module:item) is unaffected — only the resolvedPath classification moved.

expectRelationships.note: the edge is module:item and unchanged by the classification fix — pinned so a future 'fix' cannot quietly drop builtin imports from the graph
control: a package subpath keeps its package identity in the edge
